title: The Jerusalem Council
author: Jared Ludlow
author_role: Professor of Ancient Scripture, Brigham Young University

footnotes.text: Acts 15:5uses the title “sect of the Pharisees which believed” in Christ to describe some “Jewish Christians” who persisted in their desire to maintain Jewish practices as part of the Christian covenant. These were not the Pharisees frequently mentioned in the Gospels. They were Christian converts who strongly desired to maintain their Jewishness and who were probably of the Pharisaic sect before their conversion and may have maintained some connections with the Pharisees.

The takeaways from the council continued to guide the early Church. For instance, Paul later taught that circumcision and following the law of Moses were not necessary to accept Jesus Christ, even though others continued teaching these things (seeActs 21:20–21), and he repeated the four basic demands for converted Gentiles from the Jerusalem Council (seeActs 21:25).
